name: globular set

data.underlying_diagram: sequence Xn of sets, n in N, with s,t: X(n+1) -> X(n)
data.used_for: underlying graph of a strict omega-category (I.1.3(h))

quote: A globular set is a diagram ... in Set satisfying the 'globularity equations' ss = st and ts = tt : Xn+1 → Xn−1.

name: strict omega-category (informal structure)

data.composition: binary composition X(n) x_{X(k)} X(n) -> X(n) for each n>=k

quote: a strict ω-category consists of a globular set X and for each n ≥ k a binary composition function X(n) ×X(k) X(n) → X(n) and an identity function X(k) → X(n)

name: n-stage tree

data.boundary: d(tau) obtained by truncating/removing top-stage nodes
data.role: combinatorial presentation of n-globs, indexes Batanin-style composition

quote: we may define an n-stage tree (n∈N) to be a diagram τ(n) ✲ τ(n − 1) ✲ ··· ✲ τ(1) ✲ τ(0) = 1 in the category ∆ of all finite ordinals.

name: cubical set (n-cubical set)

data.index_category_Cuben: objects: subsets D of {0,...,n-1}; maps D->D': inclusion plus function D'\D -> {0,1} (0=source,1=target)
data.faces_degeneracies: coded by inclusions D subset D' with {0,1}-labelled complement, i.e. face/coface data; no degeneracy or connection maps are separately axiomatized
data.connections: not present; survey states the cubical contraction/lax theory 'has not, as far as I know, been carried out'

quote: we define an n-cubical set to be a functor Cuben op ✲ Set.

name: simplicial structure (nerve / simplicial category, not independently axiomatized)

data.role_1: category = finite-limit-preserving functor Delta^op -> Set (nerve correspondence)
data.role_2: Delta arises as free (Set/S1,T1)-structured category on the terminal multicategory 1
data.caveat: no simplicial identities or simplicial-set axioms are transcribed anywhere in the source

quote: A category is a finite-limit-preserving functor ∆op ✲ Set. In [Tam], a lax n-category is a functor (∆n)op ✲ Set satisfying three axioms.

name: opetope

data.S2: N (2-opetopes indexed by natural numbers, k-fold pasting)
data.recursion: (S(n+1) -> S(n)) = T_n(S(n) ->id S(n)); T(n+1) = free (Set/Sn,Tn)-operad monad on Set/S(n+1)
data.convention: top edges of an n-opetope are inputs, bottom edge is output

quote: In a nutshell, there is one 0-opetope and an (n + 1)-opetope is a pasting of n-opetopes.

name: opetope set construction Sn, Tn

data.S0_T0: S0 = 1, T0 = id, the identity monad on Set ≅ Set/S0
data.inductive_step: given (Sn,Tn) cartesian satisfying I.5 conditions, define Sn+1 via the terminal object construction and Tn+1 as free (Set/Sn,Tn)-operad monad
data.outputs: sequence (Set/Sn, Tn) of cartesian monads, one per dimension

quote: Start with S0 = 1 and T0 = id , the identity monad on Set∼=Set/S0

name: pasting diagram (n-pasting diagrams, PDn / pdn)

data.pdn: image of PDn under forgetful functor (Set/Sn,Tn)-Struc -> Cat
data.morphisms: removal of (n-1)-dimensional interior faces (replacement of sub-diagrams by their bounding opetope)
data.special_cases: pd0 = 1, pd1 = Delta, pd2 = category of trees

quote: The structured category of n-pasting diagrams, PDn , is the free (Set/Sn , Tn )-structured category on the terminal (Set/Sn , Tn )-multicategory.

name: category of trees (pd2)

data.identification: tree defined as 2-pasting diagram, isomorphic to the free-multicategory tree set 1* of I.1.3(f)

quote: We may define a tree to be a 2-pasting diagram: that is, a member of S3.

name: bicategory (basic notation)

data.1-cells: f, g, ... drawn as arrows between 0-cells
data.2-cells: alpha, beta, ... drawn as double arrows between parallel 1-cells
data.coherence_note: pentagon and triangle diagrams are never displayed; basic definitions cited to Benabou and Gray without restatement

quote: We will typically denote 0-cells of a bicategory B by A, B, . . . , 1-cells by f , g, . . . and 2-cells by α, β, . . .

name: bicategory pentagon axiom

data.citation: basic bicategory definitions attributed to [Ben] and [Gray] without restating pentagon

quote: The basic definitions are taken from [Bén] and [Gray], and the outline of the coherence theorem from [St2] and [GPS].

name: bicategory triangle axiom

data.citation: basic bicategory definitions attributed to [Ben] and [Gray] without restating triangle/unit law

quote: The basic definitions are taken from [Bén] and [Gray], and the outline of the coherence theorem from [St2] and [GPS].

name: unbiased category / bicategory coherence axiom

data.data_cA: function cA: C(An-1,An) x ... x C(A0,A1) -> C(A0,An) for each sequence of objects
data.1-terms: class of functions generated from the cA's by binary/nullary products and composition
data.purpose: survey's unbiased substitute for finite pentagon/triangle axiomatization

equations: s = t : C(An-1,An) x ... x C(A0,A1) -> C(A0,An), for any two 1-terms s,t
quote: The axioms are that if ... s, t: C(An−1 , An ) × · · · × C(A0 , A1 ) ✲ C(A0 , An ) are two 1-terms, then s = t.

name: monad in a bicategory

data.data: 0-cell A, 1-cell t: A->A, 2-cells eta: 1 -> t, mu: t.t -> t
data.axioms: unit and associativity squares for eta, mu commute
data.role: the general definitional device used to define (S,*)-multicategories

equations: t∘1 ≅ t∘t ≅ 1∘t via tη, ηt (unit law)
t∘(t∘t) ≅ (t∘t)∘t → t∘t → t via tµ, µt, µ (associativity)
quote: A monad in a bicategory consists of a 0-cell A, a 1-cell A ✲ A, and 2-cells [η,µ] ... such that the diagrams [unit, associativity] commute.

name: tricategory (biased, GPS-style)

data.composition: homomorphisms T(B,C) x T(A,B) -> T(A,C) and 1 -> T(A,A)
data.coherence: various coherence cells satisfying axioms (not transcribed, deferred to [GPS])

quote: A tricategory T consists of a collection T0 of objects, a bicategory T (A, B) for each pair (A, B) of objects, composition and identity homomorphisms

name: Gray-category

data.Gy_construction: Gy(tau) = Ssq(tau) for n in {0,1,2}; Gy(tau) = Ssq(d tau) x Ssq(d tau) for n=3
data.non_canonical_step: turning Gray-category into tricategory requires choosing one of two horizontal composites for 2-cells

quote: Gray-categories are defined to be algebras for the 3-operad Gy. This in turn is defined to be the 3-operad got by taking the 2-operad Ssq and contracting from dimension 2 to dimension 3.

name: sesquicategory

data.data: category C and factorization C^op x C -> Cat over ob: Set (Hom)
data.missing_structure: no specified horizontal composite of 2-cells (unlike a 2-category)

quote: for each pair of objects A, B∈C0 there is a category C(A, B) whose objects are the morphisms from A to B.

name: cartesian monad

data.cartesian_monad_condition_a: eta and mu are cartesian natural transformations (naturality squares are pullbacks)
data.role: the (S,*) machine underlying globular sets, cubical sets and opetope sets alike

quote: A monad (( )∗ , η, µ) on a category S is called cartesian if a. η and µ are cartesian natural transformations ... and b. ( )∗ preserves pullbacks.

name: (S,*)-multicategory (generalized/T-multicategory)

data.input: cartesian pair (S, *) (a cartesian category and cartesian monad)
data.kleisli_bicategory_B: 0-cells: objects of S; 1-cells R->S: spans R* <- A -> S; composed via chosen pullbacks (Construction I.2.1)
data.definition: an (S,*)-multicategory is a monad in B
data.concrete_data: diagram C0* <-d C1 ->c C0 in S plus maps ids: C0->C1, comp: C1 o C1 -> C1
data.terminology_note: the term 'T-multicategory' does not occur in this survey; its own uniform name is (S,*)-multicategory

quote: an (S, ∗ )-multicategory is a monad in the associated bicategory B of Construction I.2.1.

name: fc-multicategory (not present in this survey)

data.status: the term 'fc-multicategory' does not occur anywhere in this text
data.closest_analogue: the general (S,*)-multicategory of Definition I.2.2, instantiated at various (S,*) including (Cat, free strict monoidal category)

quote: an (S, ∗ )-multicategory is a monad in the associated bicategory B of Construction I.2.1.

name: plain multicategory

data.arrows: s1,...,sn -> s for s1,...,sn,s in C0
data.laws: composition functions and identity elements obeying associativity and unit laws

quote: The simplest kind of multicategory consists of a collection C0 of objects, and arrows like s1 , . . . , sn ✲ s, together with composition functions and identity elements obeying associativity and unit laws.

name: plain operad

data.data: sequence of sets C(0), C(1), ... plus identity element of C(1)
data.composition: C(n1) x ... x C(nk) x C(k) -> C(n1+...+nk)

quote: The simplest kind of operad—a plain operad —consists of a sequence C(0), C(1), . . . of sets together with an 'identity' element of C(1) and 'composition' functions

name: Batanin operad (as (S,*)-operad on globular sets)

data.identification: Batanin's operads and algebras are exactly (S,*)-operads/algebras for this (S,*)

quote: if S is the category of globular sets and ∗ the free strict ω-category monad, then (S, ∗ )-operads and their algebras are what Batanin calls operads and algebras.

name: contraction on a collection

data.matching_pair: (f,f') for tree sigma with s(f)=s(f') and t(f)=t(f')
data.contraction_function: psi assigning to each tau in Tr(n), n>=1, and matching pair (f,f') for d(tau), an element psi(f,f') in C(tau)
data.role: formalizes the 'contraction principle' of II.1 generating operad K

quote: A contraction ψ on C is a function assigning to each τ ∈Tr(n) and matching pair (f, f ′ ) for ∂τ , an element ψ(f, f ′ )∈C(τ )...

name: lax (weak) n-category / lax omega-category, Batanin-style (Leinster's variant)

data.operad_K: the initial operad-with-contraction on globular sets
data.lax_n_category: a lax omega-category whose underlying globular set is n-dimensional
data.n_dimensional_condition: for all m>=n, s=t: X(m+1)->X(m) is an isomorphism
data.note: author now prefers the term 'weak n-category' (preface, 2001)

quote: A lax ω-category is an algebra for K. A lax n-category is a lax ω-category whose underlying globular set is n-dimensional.

name: Tamsamani-Simpson weak n-category (described, not fully defined)

data.axiom_3: a degeneracy condition analogous to a 2-category being a double category with degenerate graph
data.status: described only in prose; formal statement not given, per the survey's own admission

quote: In [Tam], a lax n-category is a functor (∆n )op ✲ Set satisfying three axioms. ... The present author's ignorance prevents further discussion.

name: opetopic (Baez-Dolan/Hermida-Makkai-Power) weak n-category approach

data.status: the survey builds only the supporting combinatorics (opetopes, pasting diagrams, trees, slicing) and declines to restate the n-category definition itself
data.components_built: Sn/Tn opetope sets, PDn/pdn pasting-diagram categories, slice multicategory C+

quote: There is no attempt to describe the opetopic approach as a whole; the theory of Chapter I seems less well suited to this style than to Batanin's.

name: slicing / slice multicategory C+

data.output_C_plus: multicategory whose algebras are multicategories on C0 over C
data.two_step_construction: 1. slice a multicategory D by an algebra E to get D_E with Alg(D_E) = Alg(D)/E; 2. build the S-multicategory-multicategory whose algebras are multicategories on S
data.level_shift: C an (S,*)-multicategory implies C+ is an (S',#)-multicategory one level up (unlike Baez-Dolan's same-level C+, which needs symmetric group actions)

quote: Given a multicategory C, they construct a multicategory C + whose algebras are multicategories on C0 over C.

name: interchange law

data.context: two ways of composing a square built from do-nothing (0-cells) and ordinary composition (1-cells) operations
data.statement: the two composites of a 2x2 square of 2-cells (compose rows then columns, or columns then rows) agree

quote: putting these together gives two different ways of composing ... familiar from the interchange law.

name: double category

data.cells: 0-cells A, horizontal 1-cells f, vertical 1-cells p, 2-cells alpha
data.laws: strict associativity, identity, interchange for both 1-cell compositions and 2-cell composition
data.degeneracy: a 2-category is a double category in which all vertical 1-cells are identities

quote: A double category may be defined as a category object in Cat.

name: 1* : free strict omega-category on the terminal globular set 1

data.n_glob: a globular diagram representing an element of 1*(n)
data.correspondence: elements of 1*(n) correspond one-to-one with n-stage trees

quote: Having described 1∗ as a globular set, we next turn to its strict ω-category structure: in other words, how globs may be composed.

name: terminal multicategory / operad 1 and free monoidal category Delta

data.terminal_multicategory_1: one object, and for each n in N one arrow of arity n
data.free_monoidal_category: the free strict monoidal category on the terminal multicategory 1 is Delta, the category of finite ordinals, with + as tensor

quote: the 'free' monoidal category on the multicategory 1 is ∆, the category of finite ordinals (including 0), with addition as ⊗.

name: operad Ssq for sesquicategories

data.generators: one element of Ssq(tau) for each 1-stage tree and each 2-stage tree
data.relations: the sesquicategory axioms of Figure III.a
data.role: worked example of specifying an n-operad by generators and relations

quote: The 2-operad Ssq, whose algebras are sesquicategories, is generated by a single element of Ssq(τ) for the tree τ taking any one of the values [1-stage and 2-stage trees]

name: operad Gy for Gray-categories (worked example)

data.Gy_tau_dim3: Gy(tau) = Ssq(d tau) x Ssq(d tau) for n=3

quote: for τ ∈Tr(n), Gy(τ) = Ssq(τ), n∈{0, 1, 2}, Gy(τ) = Ssq(∂τ) × Ssq(∂τ), n = 3.

name: periodic table of degenerate n-categories (not present in this survey)

data.unfinished_part: no cubical analogue of 'contraction' (hence no lax n-tuple category) has been carried out
